walkthroughs.body_html: After ~18 years 11 days, the Sun-Earth-Moon geometry nearly repeats, so eclipses recur with similar properties — but shifted ~120 degrees west each cycle.
The Moon's umbra is only ~100-270 km wide. As the Moon orbits and Earth rotates, the umbra races across Earth at ~1700 km/h, so totality at one spot lasts at most ~7.5 minutes.
If the Moon is near apogee its disc looks smaller than the Sun's, so it cannot fully cover the Sun and we see an annular 'ring of fire' eclipse instead of totality.
